Museum Volunteer Memo

To all Saturday program volunteers:

The museum host team are preparing for the Saturday family program, which will run from 10 a.m. until 3 p.m. Every volunteer need to check in at the front desk before their shift begins. The desk coordinator will provide a name badge, an assignment card, and the day's emergency contact number. Volunteers assigned to the first shift should arrive fifteen minutes early for a safety briefing before the program begins.

The activity tables include clay painting paper crafts and map puzzles. Staff will cover the tables before visitors enter, but volunteers should wipe spills promptly and return unused supplies to the labeled bins. Visitors who arrives early may wait in the courtyard. If rain closes the courtyard, a staff member will direct families to the covered hall beside the main entrance.

The education room is smaller then the main gallery, so groups will enter in stages. Each activity card lists a suggested group size and the estimated time needed to finish. Please avoid promising a specific entry time when a room is full. Instead, tell visitors where the line begins and which other activities are available while they wait.

We planned the schedule carefully, however several signs still needs to be printed. The communications office expects to deliver them by Friday afternoon. Until then, the temporary signs in the supply cabinet may be used for the volunteer walk-through. Check that arrows point toward the correct room before taping a sign to a stand.

If a child loses an item please bring it to the information desk. Do not write a child's full name on the public lost-item tag; the desk attendant will record identifying information in a private log. For urgent safety concerns, contact the floor supervisor by radio.

The coordinator asked volunteers to speak clearly politely, and with patience. Families may be unfamiliar with the building, and some visitors will need extra time or directions to an accessible route. At the end of each shift, return badges and radios to the front desk and report any supply shortage before leaving.
